ORIGINAL: Web's title/description slots take ReactNode children and are explicitly styled for embedded links and multi-paragraph bodies (alert.tsx L113, L129); Flutter's Alert.title/description are plain String fields with no Widget option, so a caller cannot reproduce an in-body link or a second paragraph — a real composability loss, not just a naming difference.

api.flutter: enum AlertVariant { normal(='default'), destructive, success, warning, info } with variant.inkOf(theme) driving *:[svg] colour, and Alert.action/actionLane (space(20)=pr-20) mirroring AlertAction's absolute top-2/right-2 slot.
api.web: variant: "default"|"destructive"|"success"|"warning"|"info" (defaultVariants variant:"default"); AlertAction is `absolute top-2 right-2`, and the base gets has-data-[slot=alert-action]:pr-20 when present.
api.note: All five variant keys, the action-slot positioning (top-2/right-2 -> space(2)) and the pr-20 lane widening are reproduced 1:1 aside from the anatomy-level String-vs-Widget gap noted above.

states.flutter: Alert has exactly the five AlertVariant states and nothing else — no hover/focus/pressed/loading/disabled fields on the widget.
states.web: The alert doc page's States section marks hover, focus-visible, pressed, loading, disabled and empty all N/A, with the note "Alert is not a control — it reports, it is not operated".
states.note: Both implementations expose only the five tone variants as states; the web doc page's own N/A grid confirms no interaction states exist on either side.

disabled.flutter: Alert has no onPressed/enabled/disabled field anywhere in its constructor.
disabled.web: The alert doc page explicitly lists disabled as N/A: "Alert is not a control, it is a region that reports."
disabled.note: Alert is a passive surface on both platforms, so there is no disabled path to audit.

interaction.flutter: No GestureDetector/MouseRegion/Focus wraps Alert's build() output; only the optional `action` slot (a Button) is interactive, and that is a separate audited component.
interaction.web: Alert forwards ...props to a plain <div data-slot="alert">, with no onClick/tabIndex; only content placed in AlertAction (typically a Button) is interactive.
interaction.note: Neither Alert itself takes pointer or keyboard input on either platform; any interactivity comes from a composed Button slot audited elsewhere.

semantics.flutter: return Semantics(container: true, liveRegion: true, child: alert); applied unconditionally after the `switch (variant)` block, i.e. the SAME liveRegion:true is set for AlertVariant.normal, success, warning, destructive and info alike (alert.dart L285-291). The file's own doc table even states "role: role="alert" on the root" with no per-variant branch.
semantics.web: const ASSERTIVE_VARIANTS = new Set(["destructive", "warning"]); role={ASSERTIVE_VARIANTS.has(variant ?? "default") ? "alert" : "status"} — only destructive/warning get the assertive role="alert"; default, success and info render role="status" (polite).

ORIGINAL: This is the exact defect the web source's own comment calls out: "a page carrying an informational alert, a success alert and a warning alert interrupted the reader three times for two pieces of news that were not urgent" — Flutter's uniform liveRegion:true reproduces that interruption for every variant instead of reserving assertive announcement for destructive/warning, defeating the documented rationale. Flutter's Semantics API has no built-in polite/assertive distinction, so this needs an explicit workaround (e.g. only setting liveRegion for the two urgent variants) rather than being an unavoidable platform limit.
